title: Royal Crest Literature in English: From Page to Podium (literature + public speaking)
_note: say = text sent to ElevenLabs; cap = on-screen caption.

lines.say: Every great speech begins on a page.
lines.cap: Every great speech begins on a page.

lines.say: And every great reader can learn to speak.
lines.cap: And every great reader can learn to speak.

lines.say: Welcome to Literature in English and public speaking at Royal Crest Academy. I'm Teacher Rudo.
lines.cap: Welcome to Literature in English and public speaking at Royal Crest Academy. I’m Teacher Rudo.

lines.say: Why study literature? Because stories show us how people think, feel and change.
lines.cap: Why study literature? Because stories show us how people think, feel and change.

lines.say: And if you can explain a story clearly, you can explain almost anything.
lines.cap: And if you can explain a story clearly, you can explain almost anything.

lines.say: Let's read closely. Shakespeare, As You Like It. All the world's a stage.
lines.cap: Let’s read closely. Shakespeare, As You Like It: “All the world’s a stage.”

lines.say: That's a metaphor. Life is compared to a play.
lines.cap: That’s a metaphor. Life is compared to a play.

lines.say: Now look at one small word: merely. The men and women are merely players. It makes people sound small. That's tone.
lines.cap: Now look at one small word: “merely”. It makes people sound small. That’s tone.

lines.say: And, his acts being seven ages. The speech is built in seven parts. That's structure.
lines.cap: “His acts being seven ages”: the speech is built in seven parts. That’s structure.

lines.say: So: imagery, tone and structure. Three things to look for, every time.
lines.cap: So: imagery, tone and structure. Three things to look for, every time.

lines.say: Now turn your reading into an essay paragraph. Use peel.
lines.cap: Now turn your reading into an essay paragraph. Use PEEL.

lines.say: Point: make your claim. Evidence: a short quotation. Explain: how the words work. Link: back to the question.
lines.cap: Point: make your claim. Evidence: a short quotation. Explain: how the words work. Link: back to the question.

lines.say: Point, evidence, explain, link. A paragraph examiners love.
lines.cap: Point, Evidence, Explain, Link. A paragraph examiners love.

lines.say: On the Cambridge syllabus you'll study poetry, prose and drama, from Form One to Upper Six.
lines.cap: On the Cambridge syllabus you’ll study poetry, prose and drama, from Form 1 to Upper 6.

lines.say: But reading is only half of it. Now, say it out loud.
lines.cap: But reading is only half of it. Now, say it out loud.

lines.say: Good morning, everyone. Today I want to tell you about my favourite book, and why you should read it too.
lines.cap: Good morning, everyone. Today I want to tell you about my favourite book, and why you should read it too.

lines.say: Public speaking. Four habits of a confident speaker.
lines.cap: Public speaking. Four habits of a confident speaker.

lines.say: One: stand tall. Feet steady, shoulders relaxed.
lines.cap: 1. Stand tall. Feet steady, shoulders relaxed.

lines.say: Two: eye contact. Look at your audience, not at the floor.
lines.cap: 2. Eye contact. Look at your audience, not at the floor.

lines.say: Three: pace and pause. Slow down. A pause gives your words weight.
lines.cap: 3. Pace and pause. Slow down. A pause gives your words weight.

lines.say: Four: your voice. Loud enough for the back row, and full of feeling.
lines.cap: 4. Your voice. Loud enough for the back row, and full of feeling.

lines.say: Build every speech in three parts: a hook, the body, and a strong close.
lines.cap: Build every speech in three parts: a hook, the body and a strong close.

lines.say: Like this. Imagine a world without stories. No books, no songs, no history. Today I'll show you why stories matter.
lines.cap: “Imagine a world without stories. No books, no songs, no history. Today I’ll show you why stories matter.”

lines.say: That's a hook. Now everyone is listening.
lines.cap: That’s a hook. Now everyone is listening.

lines.say: Your turn. Give a one-minute speech on your favourite book. Hook, body, close.
lines.cap: Your turn. Give a one-minute speech on your favourite book. Hook, body, close.

lines.say: Ready? Your minute starts now.
lines.cap: Ready? Your minute starts now.

lines.say: Royal Crest Academy, Bikita. Literature in English and public speaking, on the Cambridge syllabus.
lines.cap: Royal Crest Academy, Bikita. Literature in English and public speaking, on the Cambridge syllabus.

lines.say: Read closely. Speak boldly. Form One places for twenty twenty-seven are open now.
lines.cap: Read closely. Speak boldly. Form 1 places for 2027 are open now.
